cards.q: What does the nucleus contain?
cards.a: The cell's genetic instructions, encoded in DNA.

cards.q: How does the nucleus control the cell's activities?
cards.a: By directing protein synthesis.

cards.q: What are chromosomes?
cards.a: DNA associated with many proteins. The proteins help coil the long DNA molecules.

cards.q: How long is the DNA of one human cell's 46 chromosomes?
cards.a: Over 2 m laid end to end, coiled into a nucleus only about 5 um across.

cards.q: What is chromatin?
cards.a: The complex of DNA and proteins. In a non-dividing cell it looks like a diffuse mass.

cards.q: What happens to DNA before a cell divides?
cards.a: It is copied, so each daughter cell gets an identical set of genetic instructions.

cards.q: What happens to chromatin just before cell division?
cards.a: Its fibers coil up further into thick chromosomes visible with a light microscope.

cards.q: What is the nuclear envelope?
cards.a: A double membrane around the nucleus. Each membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins.

cards.q: What do nuclear pores do?
cards.a: Protein-lined pores that regulate entry and exit of large molecules.

cards.q: The nuclear envelope connects to which membrane network?
cards.a: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER).

cards.q: What is made in the nucleolus?
cards.a: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA), made from DNA instructions.

cards.q: How are ribosomal subunits built?
cards.a: rRNA joins proteins imported from the cytoplasm. Subunits exit via pores and join in the cytoplasm.

cards.q: What is messenger RNA (mRNA)?
cards.a: A copy of protein-making instructions from DNA. It goes to the cytoplasm to be translated.

cards.q: Name the 3 processes that happen in the nucleus.
cards.a: DNA is copied; ribosomal subunits are assembled; DNA instructions are transcribed into mRNA.

cards.q: What do ribosomes do?
cards.a: Build proteins using instructions from the nucleus, written in mRNA.

cards.q: Why does a pancreas cell have millions of ribosomes?
cards.a: It makes lots of protein - digestive enzymes.

cards.q: Besides ribosomes, what is prominent in protein-making cells?
cards.a: A large nucleolus, where ribosomal subunits are assembled.

cards.q: Where are free ribosomes found?
cards.a: Suspended in the cytosol.

cards.q: Where are bound ribosomes found?
cards.a: Attached to the outside of the ER or the nuclear envelope.

cards.q: Are free and bound ribosomes different structures?
cards.a: No. They are identical and can work in either place, depending on the protein made.

cards.q: What do proteins made by free ribosomes usually do?
cards.a: Work in the cytosol, e.g. enzymes for the first steps of sugar breakdown.

cards.q: What proteins do bound ribosomes typically make?
cards.a: Proteins that will be exported from the cell.

cards.q: What does a ribosome translate mRNA into?
cards.a: The mRNA nucleotide sequence becomes the amino acid sequence of a polypeptide.

cards.q: DNA -> RNA -> protein is an example of which theme?
cards.a: The flow of INFORMATION.

cards.q: What is the endomembrane system?
cards.a: Internal membranes that work together - some physically connected, others linked by vesicles.

cards.q: Name the parts of the endomembrane system.
cards.a: Nuclear envelope, ER, Golgi, lysosomes, vesicles and vacuoles, plasma membrane.

cards.q: What are vesicles?
cards.a: Tiny sacs made of membrane that move membrane segments between organelles.

cards.q: Why is the plasma membrane in the endomembrane system?
cards.a: It is linked to the other membranes by vesicle transfer.

cards.q: What is the largest part of the endomembrane system?
cards.a: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) - a network of flattened sacs and tubules.

cards.q: What does 'endoplasmic reticulum' mean?
cards.a: Endoplasmic = 'within the cytoplasm'; reticulum = Latin for 'little net'.

cards.q: How is the ER directly connected to the nucleus?
cards.a: ER membranes are continuous with the nuclear envelope.

cards.q: How does the ER reach other organelles indirectly?
cards.a: Vesicles bud from the ER and travel to other parts of the system.

cards.q: Why does the ER enclose a space separate from the cytosol?
cards.a: It divides the cell into compartments, each able to keep different conditions.

cards.q: Which includes the rest: ER, vesicle, endomembrane system, nuclear envelope?
cards.a: The endomembrane system.
